title: Signal Fusion: prioritization engine for model landscape & competitive gaps
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight prioritization engine (Signal Fusion) that ingests model release metadata, observed latency/cost telemetry, customer incident reports, and public competitive signals to output a ranked list of candidate models/variants for onboarding, fallback, or cadence monitoring. Goals: 1) reduce time-to-decision for model onboarding by surfacing high-opportunity, low-friction candidates; 2) surface early regression signals tied to specific model versions; 3) provide a repeatable scoring rubric PMs and Eng can use to justify prioritization and capacity planning.
updates:
2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting with Eng (Marco, Priya), Research (Loren), and DS (Yujin). Agreed scope: initial MVP limited to open-model releases + internal telemetry. Action: eng to provide sample telemetry table by 2026-02-20.
2026-02-22: Received telemetry schema from ENG-5873. Noted mismatch on tokenization granularity; decision to normalize to per-request latency and per-embedding time.
2026-03-01: Draft scoring rubric v0.1 uploaded to Confluence (link below). PM/Eng review flagged weight on "cost delta" too high; adjusted weights (capex sensitivity reduced).
2026-03-05: DS provided prototype aggregator notebook (GH PR: redwood/signal-agg#214). Performance tests show full run for 90 days completes in ~22 minutes on dev infra.
2026-03-10: Design review with Solutions and SE (Rachel). Feedback: include customer-facing severity mapping and link to incident playbooks for high-priority regressions. Added follow-up task to integrate CS incident labels.
2026-03-12: Executive sync — agreed to run pilot on two candidate models (open-llm-x-small64 and opt-rolling-3b-quant) for embeddings latency arbitration. Updated due_date to 2026-04-01 for pilot completion.
decision_log: Trade-offs considered: (A) Heavy-weight ML classifier to predict customer churn vs (B) deterministic score that is transparent to PM/Eng. Chosen approach: deterministic, explainable score for MVP to accelerate adoption and reviewability. Scoring formula components: observed latency percentile, cost-per-token delta vs baseline, public capability signal (binary), customer incident count (weighted by severity), and quantization incompatibility flag. Weights locked for MVP; plan to AB test weightings in Q2 after pilot.

DS: augment prototype to include incident severity mapping and output per-candidate rationale strings (owner: Yujin) by 2026-03-20

notes: Do not conflate 'high score' with immediate onboarding — prioritized list requires capacity check and legal/compliance signoffs for non-open models. Consider integrating model licensing and quantization readiness into phase 2. Also track regional availability (APAC EU) as a filter in the prioritizer for enterprise customers.
